A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TPDM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including v2's added Appendix C and Table 4.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation evaluations, a 15-volunteer user study, TPM input ablations and scheduling sensitivity analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 4–6.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds an original Stable Diffusion 1.5 scheduler comparison in Appendix C, Table 4.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds a DDPM adaptation that quantizes TPM's predicted diffusion time to an available discrete step and obtains its corresponding noise level, with integration into DPM-Solver++. The existing TPM architecture, Beta-distribution predictor and reinforcement-learning objective remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources and the text-to-image task are retained. V2 first names 5,000 COCO 2017 validation prompts for Table 4 and says it follows Table 1's protocol, but v1 does not identify its quantitative evaluation dataset. The PDFs therefore do not establish whether evaluation data coverage expanded or was merely disclosed.

E2.justification: V1 principally compares TPDM with its backbone models using fixed schedules. V2 retains those comparisons and adds DPM-Solver++ alone, DPM-Solver++ with AYS, and DPM-Solver++ with GITS in Table 4. This substantially broadens comparison to competing scheduling methods; AYS was previously cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces approximately 200 training steps with 200 sampled trajectories and four PPO epochs, retaining batch size 256. This changes the reported training specification without establishing that experiments were rerun. Table 4 also introduces the SD1.5/DPM-Solver++ configuration with 10-step comparators; existing metrics and user-study settings are retained.

E4.justification: The prompt-complexity analysis in Figure 4, qualitative comparisons in Figure 5, discount-factor sensitivity in Figure 6 and layer-input ablation in Table 3 are retained. Table 4 adds benchmark comparisons rather than a separate ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without evaluation seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added Table 4 follows this practice; PPO epochs and sampled training trajectories are not repeated evaluation runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their values. New Table 4 reports TPM FID 18.31 at 9.890 average steps, versus 21.08, 18.81 and 18.32 for 10-step DPM-Solver++, AYS and GITS configurations. Figure 1 also changes several reported inference counts, including the deep-sea image from 20 to 12. These are added results and revised annotations, not demonstrated same-setting improvements between versions.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds Equations 10–13 defining the discrete DDPM variance schedule, cumulative signal coefficient and corresponding noise level. Equations 1–9 and their mathematical reasoning remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list and conclusion retain the same adaptive-scheduling, reinforcement-learning and quality-versus-efficiency claims, including the headline SD3 scores and approximately 50% fewer steps. The DDPM experiment supports the existing general-applicability claim.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds interpretations concerning compatibility with DDPMs and higher-order solvers, and argues that GITS's use of evaluation-set statistics limits benefits for single-image generation. Its claim of superiority over GITS across all metrics exceeds Table 4's reported CLIP-T tie. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds four PPO epochs to the training description and documents the DDPM time/noise mapping, a typical diffusion training horizon of 1,000 steps, and the 5,000-prompt COCO evaluation sample. The existing prompt-filtering appendix and promise of a future model release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 substantially revises research positioning: it adds DDPO, DPOK, DACER and Diffusion-DPO, withdraws the broad first-to-treat-denoising-steps-as-RL-actions assertion, and distinguishes time actions from latent actions. Additional references cover GITS, DPM-Solver++, latent diffusion and molecular scheduling. This changes the account of closely related work and the basis of the claimed distinction.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites Section 2.3, adds short passages in Sections 2.2 and 4.3, appends Section C, and adjusts an author affiliation. Most prose, section ordering and the main narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 4 and moves Figure 8 upward to accommodate Appendix C. Figure 5 loses its panel letters and changes model headers to 'SD3-Median', although the caption still identifies SD3-Medium. Existing diagrams, plots and main table structures are retained, with limited page reflow.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the paper through direct comparisons with competing schedulers, an explicit DDPM adaptation and more precise positioning against prior RL work. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: Table 4 implies a 2.77 FID reduction rather than the claimed 2.79, and the all-metric superiority statement overlooks a reported CLIP-T tie. The central results and analyses remain unchanged, making the overall improvement incremental.
